note: Gathering on foot (docs/future/13-keepers-camp.md 4.2, 4.4, 4.5; src/world/gather/). reachM: arm's reach (m) for a Gather; waterReachM: into water from the bank (lily leaves, pondweed). nearLookM: ground that is everywhere (sand, pebbles, flat stones, a strandline stretch) opens its card when tapped within this many meters of the walker; a tap further off just walks (Matt, 2026-10-22). kneelS: the kneel for one handful; approachTimeoutS: how long the walk to a spot may take before it gives up. eventCap: the most picked spots the save remembers (oldest go first). spotM: the side of a ground spot's bin (m), over the 0.5 m water cells. marksMax: picked-over marks drawn near the view. plants: regrowth model B. A pick sets size = max(floor x best, size x (1 - share)); a plant is pickable when it has been mature (best at least matureSize), its size is at least readyShare x best, and the part is in its season window. While size < readyShare x best, a picked plant's hourly growth is multiplied by recoverRate x (1 + rainBoost x rain + mistBoost x mist), rain and mist this hour's (weather now). defaults: share and readyShare by part type. parts: one entry per gatherable plant part, keyed '<species>.<part>', naming its type (for the defaults) and its window as season positions [from, to) (0 spring .. 4, wrapping, as flora recipes' flowering and dormant windows), read on the world's calendar (the season the island shows); its own share or readyShare overrides the type's; a part picked twice a year lists both windows, [[from, to), [from, to)]. Reed down: late autumn into winter. weather: windyMin is the day record's windStrength for a windy day (today or yesterday); onshoreDot: a tide's day is onshore when dot(windToward, outward) is at most this, windToward = (cos windDir, -sin windDir), outward from the island's centre to the stretch; springMin: how far toward spring a line's tide must be for cast kelp. A fire-night (the ring's charcoal and ash) is camp.json fire.night. bins: steepDeg is the slope (degrees) at which sand on the shore counts as shingle; ankleM is the deepest a stream bed's water may be for pebbles; tapM, how near its cell (m) a tap must land to find a bin's spot. strand: toleranceM, how far (m) a cell's ground may sit from a line's level (plus the shore recipe's runupM) and still be on it. kinds: one per ground kind (Phase 1: sticks, drift twigs, pebbles, flat stones). source is where it lies (foot of a host plant, a ground bin, a strandline stretch); handfuls and empty are by season (spring, summer, autumn, winter): empty is the share of spots holding nothing that period, otherwise a spot holds handfuls plus the modifiers. sticks: hosts and hostMin (the least stage of the host); windy adds that many on a windy day (today or yesterday), when empty is emptyWindy instead. drift-twigs: lines is how many of the newest lines carry them; onshore adds that many when the tide's day was onshore, when empty is emptyOnshore. pebbles and flat stones: where names the ground they lie on (shoreShingle: sand or shingle in or above the tide band; streamBed: running or slow fresh water no deeper than ankleM; bandRock: rock in the tide band; steepShingle: shore sand at least steepDeg steep). cluster (F6, Matt, October 23, 2026: about a fifth as many as before): a beach kind lies in a few natural clusters, its bins grouped in cells of cellBins a side and a cell kept with chance keep (a strandline's clusters move with each tide); nearBoat: within radiusM of where the boat lands the keeper every bin is in play, with these empty shares, so the first evening always has drift twigs and stones close by. Strandline halved (Matt, October 26, 2026: far too busy): the strand kinds keep half the clusters they did (drift twigs, shells and kelp 0.175, wrack 0.225), and near the boat each strand kind lies in about half the bins it would otherwise (kelp, wrack and shells half their usual share; drift twigs 0.65 empty, was 0.5, a little less than half so the first evening still finds its two handfuls on nearly every seed), so the seasons and onshore blows keep their proportions away from the boat. words: the card's lines. Out of season (plants.js outOfSeasonLine), a dormant plant says resting; any other says nothingNow and when the part comes: comes[part] (or comes.default) with {when} said against the season the island shows: soon within soonDays game days, later this {season} if it opens further on in this same season, else the third of the season its window opens in (when, twelve thirds from early spring). Part windows are read on the world's calendar, the one the island shows. lookOnly (docs/future/13 PR-44): plants never gathered; their card says notForDrinking with Leave it be, and the first time the walker meets one, refused[plant] shows for refusedS seconds and its page learns why. The four tea herbs (P2b, docs/future/13 5.4): water mint leaves mid spring to autumn, meadowsweet flowers in high summer, nettle tops in spring and again in autumn, chamomile flowers summer into early autumn. Winter picks (docs/future/13 5.2): gorse flowers all year, willow withies and bark all winter; reed down from autumn, when the seed heads turn brown, into winter.

plants.seedNote: Seed saving (P2g G1, D1b): a plant past bloom gives its seed, one handful a pouch sowing, once in a while (type seed: a gather takes share of its size, ready again at readyShare). Windows run from the end of its flowering to the autumn. Iris and marsh marigold are never picked (lookOnly), but their seed is saved. A seed part out of its window says nothing on the card.

reeds.leaves.note: October 28, 2026 (Matt): reed leaves from mid spring into autumn, twisted into rush cord at the workbench (cook.json), so cord never waits on rushes coming.

lilies.leaf.note: October 27, 2026: a lily leaf for the turtles' parcel (cook.json lily-parcel), picked in summer from the bank or the shallows (waterReachM): a pick takes the water type's share and the plant grows it back.

cover.note: Cover plants picked by the cell (docs/future/13 4.2, P2c C1): a pick lowers the 1 m cell's share by coverShare of full, and it grows back toward what the ground supports at the cover's own rate (about a day or two). A cell can be picked while its share is at least readyShare of that target and at least minShare of full. species: each cover plant that gives a part, its part and window (season positions, as plant parts), and the line its card says out of season. October 29, 2026 (Matt): a young or spreading bed must give stems too, so readyShare is 0 and only minShare rests a cell (a full cell gives three picks, then rests).

rushes.outOfSeason: Sodden through the winter. Last year's stems dry out by spring.
rushes.note: October 28, 2026 (Matt): spring rushes give last year's dry stems, good for cord, so the first season is never without it; the green stems follow in summer. Winter stays closed.

cover.seedNote: seedWindow (P2g G1): when a cover plant's stand gives its seed as well, with no share taken.

sand.note: P2c: dry sand above the wet line, three handfuls a 2 m bin a day, none on a rain day or the day after (rainNone). hereOnly: the ground itself is never clicked (docs/future/13 3.12); it is offered as Scoop sand on the here-bar while you stand on it (src/world/dig).

shells.note: S2: broken shells along the newest two strandlines, more after an onshore blow and in winter storms; ground to crushed shell at the apothecary (Grind).

charcoal.note: P2i: lumps of charcoal at the fire ring's edge the morning after a fire-night (camp.json fire.night), from dawn until the next dusk. Never rolled: a fire-night always leaves them.

ash.note: P2i: soft wood ash in the ring the morning after a fire-night, as charcoal. spread: Spread here on the ash pouch's card tips a handful where you stand: a pale patch patchM across lies there for days game days (at most max at once, the oldest going first), and nettles already on the island may spread onto it (src/world/growth/volunteers.js ashSpread). It guides a plant that came by itself; it never brings a new one. look: the patch drawn into the ground (lib-holes.wgsl, after the dug holes): wood ash's linear albedo, how strongly it covers the ground when fresh (it settles to about a third of that over its days), and how near the view it is drawn.

kelp.note: P2h: cast kelp along the newest two strandlines, only from a tide at least weather.springMin toward spring (spring: true), more after an onshore blow and in winter storms. The frogs' treat, with wrack; P2g lays it in planting holes.

wrack.note: P2h: dried wrack along the newest two strandlines, on any tide, more after an onshore blow. The frogs' treat; P2g lays it in planting holes.

leaves.note: P2h: fallen leaves under the willows from autumn into early winter (willow leafFall), more after a windy day. Made into a leaf pack with rush cord at the workbench (cook.json).

words.strandPicked: Picked over. The next tide will bring more.
words.young: Still small. Let it grow first.
words.holding: It is holding on to the rock. Leave it be.
words.above: You can gather this on foot.
words.sleepers: Frogs sleep in the mud here.
words.tooBig: Too big to lift. It is rooted deep.

refused.iris: Not this one. Iris root is poison, so I only look.
refused.marigold: Not this one. Its sap blisters the hands, so I only look.

words.acorns: Too bitter. These are for the jay.
words.ashSpread: A handful of ash, tipped out pale on the ground.
